name: repair_wrong_containment_param
prompt: This playbook ran on the box and the run reported Success, but nothing was ever banned on the firewall -- the FortiGate step came back with `newly_blocked`, `already_blocked`, `error_with_block` and `vdom_not_exist` all empty. Find the defect and return the corrected complete YAML. Change nothing else.
notes: Second repair defect class: `block_ip_new` called Address Based with the singular `ip`, which on a real appliance answers Success and bans nothing (live-verified on the lab FortiGate -- every result bucket empty). This is the SYMPTOM the prompt describes, and the fixture grades whether the agent restores the Quarantine Based / `ip_addresses` shape rather than deleting the step. The compiler already sees this one -- it raises `param-set conflict on fortigate-firewall.block_ip_new`, so the broken state fails `draft`, same tier as `repair_bad_step_ref`. That was NOT assumed; it was measured while calibrating, and it is worth knowing: a defect that costs a live containment is statically detectable today. The tier that no static gate can see is covered by `repair_loop_over_wrong_field`. The tempting wrong fixes here are destructive -- drop the block, or replace containment with a comment; both clear every diagnostic and are caught only by `no_collateral_damage`.

ir_assertions.note: containment passes the plural `ip_addresses` param, not `ip`
the only block_ip_new branch that bans anything
the block step is still there -- not deleted to silence it
the approval gate still precedes the block -- a fix must not reroute it
